steps.narration: First find the molar mass. Two irons at 56 and three oxygens at 16 give 160.
Divide the mass by the molar mass. 80 over 160 is half a mole.
Each Fe₂O₃ holds two iron atoms, so half a mole gives one whole mole of iron.
Multiply by 56. One mole of iron weighs 56 grams. That is the answer.
Moles equal mass divided by molar mass.
Put in the mass, 4.6 grams, over sodium's molar mass, 23.
4.6 divided by 23 is 0.2. So there are 0.2 moles of sodium.
Count the atoms. One calcium, one carbon and three oxygens.
Multiply each atom by its mass. Three oxygens at 16 each.
Add them up. 40 plus 12 plus 48 is 100.
At s.t.p., volume equals moles times 22.4.
Put in 0.25 moles.
A quarter of 22.4 is 5.6 cubic decimetres.
Calcium carbonate has a molar mass of 100, so 50 grams is half a mole.
One calcium carbonate gives one calcium oxide, so we get half a mole of CaO.
Calcium oxide has a molar mass of 40 plus 16, which is 56.
Half of 56 is 28. So 28 grams of calcium oxide form.
First find moles. 4 grams over 40 is 0.1 mole.
Change cubic centimetres to cubic decimetres. 500 over 1000 is 0.5.
Concentration is moles over volume. 0.1 over 0.5 is 0.2 moles per cubic decimetre.
Count the atoms. There are two nitrogens, one in each part.
28 for nitrogen, 4 for hydrogen and 48 for oxygen make 80.
Nitrogen is 28 out of 80.
28 over 80, times 100, is 35 percent.
Write the cathode equation. Each copper ion takes two electrons.
So two moles of electrons deposit one mole of copper.
We have 0.2 moles of electrons, so we get 0.1 moles of copper.
0.1 times 64 is 6.4 grams of copper.
At constant temperature, pressure times volume stays the same.
Put in the first pressure and volume, and the new pressure of 2.
Divide 200 by 2. The new volume is 100 cubic centimetres.
Hydrochloric acid ionises fully, so the hydrogen ion concentration is 0.01.
Write 0.01 as 10 to the power minus 2.
pH is minus the log, so the pH is 2.
